$comment: Single source for the participant card (CARD.md) and the hub (hub/index.html). Edit this file, then run npm run card. npm run card:check fails when the generated files are out of date. Plain English, one idea per sentence.
title: Workshop 5 · AI SRE first responder

start.say: Create the isolated starter from committed HEAD. Keep the lab terminal open. Use a second terminal for everything else.
stuck: Port 4310 or 4320 is already in use
Another copy runs. Stop only your own workshop launcher with Ctrl+C in its terminal. Never kill an unknown process.
Install Node 22 or newer. Check with `node --version`.
The console header says no telemetry
Wait 20 seconds. The shop writes telemetry every few seconds while traffic runs.

cores.name: Investigate the evidence
cores.goal: Break the shop, let the console raise an incident, and check every claim in the diagnosis against the data. Find what the agent cannot see.
cores.slides: Core 1: Investigate the evidence · Core 1: Check the claims

steps.do: Break the shop once: click `Bad deploy v2.15.0` in the shop OR run `npm run chaos -- deploy v2.15.0 --mode bad-deploy` in your second terminal. Do not do both.
steps.see: After about one minute a new incident appears in the console sidebar. You did not open it; the deterministic listener did.
steps.stuck: No incident after three minutes: look at the lab terminal. Traffic must print requests. Started without `--fast`? Then detection takes five minutes.

steps.do: Open the incident. Read the banner at the top, then the diagnosis.
steps.see: The diagnosis proposes `investigate-more` with low confidence. Under Data gaps it says `list_deploys: no deploys in the window`.
steps.check: Find each reference in `demo/data/telemetry.json`. Then search that file for `v2.15.0`: there WAS a deploy. The agent cannot see it, and it says so.
steps.stuck: References are text, not links. Search the file for the timestamp.

steps.do: Challenge the agent in chat: Could this be something other than the deployment?
steps.see: Offline, the agent returns a scripted summary. It is not a new model investigation.
steps.check: Compare its answer with `ruled_out` and the data gap. A missing signal is unknown, not healthy: that is why the agent does not propose a rollback.
steps.stuck: Chat refuses your sentence: that is correct for anything that changes the system. Approve, execute and resolve are buttons.

steps.do: Save the diagnosis in `docs/diagnosis-live.md`. Then record what you checked: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 1: <what you verified>"`
steps.see: One new line at the bottom of `PROGRESS.md`.
steps.check: Your note names the references you checked, not only that you did it.
steps.stuck: Do not approve. There is nothing safe to execute yet. Core 2 gives the agent its eyes back.

cores.name: Build a change safely and test it
cores.goal: Rebuild the read-only `list_deploys` tool test-first, prove it with the tests and the bench, and watch the diagnosis change.
cores.slides: Core 2: Build a change safely · Core 2: Prove it on the live incident

steps.do: Run the red test: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts`
steps.see: The test fails: `list_deploys` returns nothing. `npm run bench` fails too: without deploys the agent misses the bad deploy.
steps.check: Read the failing assertion before you change code. Say in one sentence why it fails.
steps.stuck: Find the single `TODO(A5)` handler stub in `src/tools.ts`. Restore its handler binding AND the MCP registration; the registration has an explanatory comment, not a second TODO marker.

steps.do: Build `list_deploys` in `src/tools.ts` with Claude Code or by hand. Bind the handler AND register the tool.
steps.see: `test/workshop/tools.test.ts` is green. The A8 valid-approval executor assertion remains red until Core 3.
steps.check: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run bench` pass. The bench prints `PASS bench`. Executor tests remain expected to fail until Core 3 restores the approval gate.
steps.stuck: The tool still returns `[]`: you did only one of the two halves.

steps.do: Save. In the same incident, ask in chat: `Investigate: customers report checkout errors`
steps.see: The lab terminal prints a console reload line. The new diagnosis proposes `rollback` with no data gap, and the banner says Approve or reject “rollback”.
steps.check: The diagnosis cites `deploys:<id>` for `v2.15.0`. Record it: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 2: …"`
steps.stuck: Incident gone? Incident history persists in SQLite, while the shop resets on restart. Do not restart the launcher to reload code; saving auto-reloads the console. For a fresh repeat, use a new disposable checkpoint copy; do not rebreak a stale incident.

cores.name: Judge the recovery
cores.goal: Rebuild the approval gate, sign the rollback with your name, and decide from the recovery checks whether the incident may close.
cores.slides: Core 3: Judge the recovery · Core 3: Close it, or stop safely

steps.do: Run the red test: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/executor.test.ts`. Rebuild `checkApproval` in `src/executor.ts` (`TODO(A8)`).
steps.see: The test is green. The executor now refuses to act without a named approval for this incident and this proposal.
steps.check: `npm run verify` and `npm run test:workshop` pass before a human approves the rollback. The console reloads by itself.
steps.stuck: Read `test/workshop/executor.test.ts`. It names every case the gate must refuse.

steps.do: Open your incident. The banner says Approve or reject “rollback”. Type your name. Click Approve, then Execute rollback.
steps.see: The banner says Wait: recovery checks are running. About two minutes later it says LANDED or NOT LANDED.
steps.check: The half check may fail. The full and double checks must both pass. On NOT LANDED the banner names the failed check, its value and the limit.
steps.stuck: A button is grey: the banner says which step is allowed now. The server refuses every other button.

steps.do: LANDED: click Mark mitigated, then Resolve with notes. NOT LANDED: do not close. Read the failed check, then investigate in chat or escalate.
steps.see: After you resolve, the next-step detail says Resolved and directs you to the notes and lesson. Execute stays disabled.
steps.check: `lessons/lessons.md` has a new entry with your name and the incident id. Record it: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 3: …"`
steps.stuck: Never execute again to get a green result. NOT LANDED is a correct, safe stop.

deeper.name: Write your team intent.md
deeper.do: Fill `intent.md`: who the agent serves, the boundary, and three checks a stranger can verify. The design-control-loop skill can interview you.

deeper.name: Read the contract
deeper.do: Write `docs/spec.md` for the evidence rules in `src/contract.ts`. Run `npx tsx --test test/contract.test.ts` and break one rule on purpose.

deeper.name: Add your own guard rule
deeper.do: Add one deny rule of your own to `.claude/hooks/guard.mjs` BY HAND (the agent may not edit hooks). Prove it with a deny line in `approvals/audit.jsonl`. Write `docs/decisions/D01-*.md`.

deeper.name: Add a bench case
deeper.do: Add one case to `bench/cases.json`, run `npm run bench`. Ask the agent to lower `bench/ratchet.json` and watch the guard deny it.

deeper.name: The git gate
deeper.do: Ask the agent to push `fix/<your-name>`: denied. Your neighbour runs `npm run approve:git -- <their-name> fix/<your-name> "<reason>"` in their own terminal.

deeper.name: Your hackathon intent.md
deeper.do: Write `docs/hackathon-intent.md` for the agent you build next. Hand off with the `/handoff` skill.

checkpoints.say: The committed-HEAD starter has the A5 tool exercise and a fail-closed A8 approval gate.
Core 2 retains the solved read-only tool and the fail-closed A8 approval gate.
Core 3 is the solved committed HEAD with no exercise cuts.

catchUp: Run `npm run checkpoint -- core-2` or `npm run checkpoint -- core-3` from any starter copy. Each creates a separate current-HEAD worktree under `.lab/checkpoints/` and refuses to overwrite an existing destination. Your files remain unchanged. Never copy runtime data, approvals, progress, or lesson history.
